citations.F1: N+1 query — `serialize_event` runs one `SELECT ... FROM users` per event, 1,912 sequential round trips per request; fetch all actors in one `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: Dedupe loop is O(n²) — `seen` is a list, so `ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` is a linear scan, ~1.8M comparisons at 1,912 rows
citations.F3: Blocking call in the async path — `requests.get` in `lookup_geo` is synchronous and stalls the whole worker's event loop for up to 2 s per uncached IP
citations.F4: add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` grows forever for *every* request on every route ... replace with a bounded `collections.deque(maxlen=...)`
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict keyed on client IP with no eviction; bound it (`functools.lru_cache` or a size-capped dict with TTL)
citations.F7: Baseline first: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` the events SELECT for org 4127, and time the endpoint 5× warm against acme's 1,912-event window ... Re-run the step-2 measurement after each of steps 3, 4, 6, 7 separately
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal — item 1 gives 16 workers × 50 conns × 6 pods = 4,800 Postgres connections ... and multiplies the per-worker memory leak by 4; item 2 never hits
citations.F11: item 2 never hits, because `since` defaults to `datetime.now()` so every cache key is unique
